\begin{abstract}
We introduce a model of reflective research in which the admissible outcome at each stage depends on the current research cycle. A system consists of a cycle space $C$, an indexed family $E(c)$ of outcome spaces, a revision operation $R(c,e)$, and a natural-valued quality function $q$. We assume that quality is nondecreasing under every revision, bounded by a finite capacity $K$, and extensionally stable at plateaus: if a revision produces no quality increase, it leaves the entire cycle unchanged. We prove that quality along every run is monotone, equality of consecutive quality values forces equality of consecutive cycles, and every run is eventually constant. Consequently, in any discrete topology on $C$, the trajectory converges to its eventual value. Every outcome selected after stabilization also fixes the limiting cycle. The argument supplies an order--topology bridge from the ascending-chain condition for bounded subsets of $\N$ to exact stabilization in a dependent state space.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Reflective processes can revise the framework in which their next step is interpreted. A research cycle may alter its hypotheses, vocabulary, protocol, or standard of evidence. Hence the outcome available at stage $n+1$ need not belong to the same space as the outcome available at stage $n$. A fixed update map conceals this dependence by placing all possible inputs in one ambient set, including inputs meaningless at most states.

The natural structure is an indexed family. If $c$ is a current cycle, $E(c)$ is the space of outcomes meaningful at $c$. A revision accepts $(c,e)$ with $e\in E(c)$ and returns a new cycle. State dependence alone gives no convergence. We therefore add a bounded quality rank. Revision never lowers rank, and equality of rank across a revision forces equality of the complete cycles. This last plateau condition transfers stationarity from a coarse numerical observable to the rich state.

Our conclusion is exact: every run eventually reaches a cycle that persists forever. No finiteness is imposed on the cycle space or individual outcome spaces. Only the quality range is bounded in $\N$.

\section{Mathematical framework}

\begin{definition}[Reflective research system]
A reflective research system is a tuple
\[
\System=(C,E,R,q,K)
\]
with the following data and laws. The set $C$ consists of cycles. For each $c\in C$, $E(c)$ is the set of admissible outcomes at $c$. Revision is a dependent operation
\[
R:\prod_{c\in C}E(c)\longrightarrow C,
\]
so $R(c,e)\in C$ whenever $e\in E(c)$. Quality is a map $q:C\to\N$, and $K\in\N$ is a capacity satisfying
\[
q(c)\le K.
\]
For every $c\in C$ and $e\in E(c)$, revision is quality-monotone,
\[
q(c)\le q(R(c,e)),
\]
and plateau-stable,
\[
q(R(c,e))=q(c)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R(c,e)=c.
\]
\end{definition}

The capacity bounds quality, not the cardinality or complexity of $C$. The indexed family is essential: a revision may change which outcomes are meaningful next.

\begin{definition}[Dependent run]
A run of $\System$ is a pair of sequences $(c_n)_{n\in\N}$ and $(e_n)_{n\in\N}$ satisfying
\[
e_n\in E(c_n),\qquad c_{n+1}=R(c_n,e_n)
\]
for every $n\in\N$. Its quality sequence is $a_n=q(c_n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Eventual constancy]
A sequence $(c_n)$ is eventually constant if there are $N\in\N$ and $c_*\in C$ such that $c_n=c_*$ for every $n\ge N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Discrete convergence]
The discrete topology on $C$ is the topology in which every subset is open. A sequence converges to $c_*$ if every neighborhood of $c_*$ contains all sufficiently late terms.
\end{definition}

In a discrete topology, convergence to $c_*$ is equivalent to eventual equality with $c_*$, since the singleton $\{c_*\}$ is a neighborhood.

\section{Order-theoretic lemmas}

\begin{lemma}[Quality monotonicity]
For every run, if $i\le j$, then $a_i\le a_j$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For one step, the evolution equation and revision monotonicity give
\[
a_n=q(c_n)\le q(R(c_n,e_n))=q(c_{n+1})=a_{n+1}.
\]
Chaining these inequalities from $i$ to $j$ proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Plateau step]
If $a_{n+1}=a_n$, then $c_{n+1}=c_n$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Substitute $c_{n+1}=R(c_n,e_n)$ into the equality of ranks and apply plateau stability.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Attained maximum]
If $(a_n)$ is a sequence in $\N$ with $a_n\le K$ for every $n$, then its set of attained values has a maximum $L$, and $L=a_N$ for some $N$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The attained set is nonempty and contained in the finite ordered set $\{0,1,\ldots,K\}$. It therefore has a maximum, which by definition is attained.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Eventual constancy of bounded monotone ranks]
If $(a_n)$ is monotone and bounded above by $K$, then there are $N,L\in\N$ such that $a_n=L$ for every $n\ge N$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $L=a_N$ be the attained maximum. For $n\ge N$, monotonicity gives $L=a_N\le a_n$, while maximality gives $a_n\le L$. Hence $a_n=L$.
\end{proof}

\section{Main results}

\begin{theorem}[Eventual Stabilization and Discrete Convergence]
Let $\System=(C,E,R,q,K)$ be a reflective research system and $(c_n,e_n)$ any dependent run. There exists $N\in\N$ such that
\[
c_n=c_N\qquad\text{for every }n\ge N.
\]
If $C$ carries a discrete topology, then $c_n\to c_N$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The quality sequence is monotone and bounded by $K$, so the preceding lemma gives $N$ and $L$ with $a_n=L$ for all $n\ge N$. Thus $a_{n+1}=a_n$ for every $n\ge N$. The plateau-step lemma gives $c_{n+1}=c_n$ for every such $n$. Induction yields $c_{N+m}=c_N$ for all $m\in\N$, proving eventual constancy. Every neighborhood of $c_N$ contains $c_N$, hence it contains every term from time $N$ onward; this is convergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Eventual fixedness under selected outcomes]
Under the same hypotheses, there exists $N\in\N$ such that for every $n\ge N$,
\[
R(c_n,e_n)=c_n.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose $N$ from the stabilization theorem. For $n\ge N$, both $c_n$ and $c_{n+1}$ equal $c_N$. The evolution equation gives $R(c_n,e_n)=c_{n+1}=c_n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bound on strict revisions]
Along a run beginning at $c_0$, the number of indices $n$ satisfying $c_{n+1}\ne c_n$ is at most $K-q(c_0)$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
A nonidentity revision cannot preserve rank by plateau stability, and cannot lower rank by monotonicity. It therefore increases the natural rank by at least one. The rank begins at $q(c_0)$ and never exceeds $K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Selected-outcome fixedness is run-relative. It does not claim that $R(c_N,e)=c_N$ for every $e\in E(c_N)$. An unselected outcome may still strictly increase rank. Universal fixedness requires fairness or a local maximality assumption.
\end{remark}

\section{Algorithms and examples}

\subsection{Trace validation and stabilization detection}

Given a finite prefix of length $T$, evaluate each revision and quality, verify the evolution equation, check
\[
q(c_n)\le q(c_{n+1})\le K,
\]
and require equality of adjacent ranks to imply equality of cycles. This takes $O(T)$ evaluations and $O(1)$ auxiliary space when streamed. It validates the observed trace, not unobserved revisions.

If the global hypotheses are known, equality $q(c_{n+1})=q(c_n)$ certifies that this particular step is fixed. For a finite report, one may locate the earliest index after the last strict rank increase. Full reporting uses $O(T)$ storage; retaining only the last increase uses $O(1)$ storage.

\begin{example}[Dependent finite-capacity system]
Fix $K\in\N$ and let
\[
C=\{0,1,\ldots,K\},\qquad E(r)=\{0,1,\ldots,K-r\}.
\]
For an admissible gain $g\in E(r)$, set
\[
R(r,g)=r+g,\qquad q(r)=r.
\]
The hypotheses hold. With $K=8$, $c_0=1$, and gains $2,1,3,1,0,0,\ldots$, the cycles are
\[
1,3,4,7,8,8,8,\ldots.
\]
The outcome spaces change from $E(1)=\{0,\ldots,7\}$ to $E(7)=\{0,1\}$ and finally $E(8)=\{0\}$.
\end{example}

\begin{example}[Richer protocols]
Let a cycle be $(r,p)$, where $r\in\{0,\ldots,K\}$ is quality and $p$ a protocol label. A valid revision either strictly raises $r$ and may change $p$, or leaves both coordinates unchanged. Quality need not uniquely identify cycles, but equal-ranked motion is forbidden. The theorem stabilizes both rank and protocol.
\end{example}

\section{Necessity and scope}

Each hypothesis blocks a separate failure. Without monotonicity, two states of ranks $0$ and $1$ may alternate. Without boundedness, the run $0,1,2,\ldots$ increases forever. Without plateau stability, two distinct states of rank $0$ may alternate while quality remains bounded and constant. Thus convergence of a coarse observable does not imply convergence of the object unless equal-ranked transitions are rigid.

The theorem needs neither finite $C$ nor finite $E(c)$, and it assumes no metric, compactness, deterministic selection, or decidable equality. The finite object is the interval of ranks.

\section{Applications and interpretation}

In adaptive science, a cycle can encode a theory, design, and acceptance criteria; outcomes depend on the active design. In self-revising software, a cycle can contain code and its future test policy. In logical reflection, cycles can be theories and outcomes can be theory-indexed certificates or countermodels. In governance, changing evaluation rules changes which proposals are admissible. In every interpretation, a bounded milestone rank acts as a progress certificate, while plateau stability forbids cosmetic rank-neutral changes.

The argument is an ascending-chain proof. Every genuine state change induces a strict ascent in $\{0,\ldots,K\}$. Equivalently, remaining capacity $V(c)=K-q(c)$ is a nonincreasing termination variant and strictly decreases on every genuine change. The rank also resembles a Lyapunov function with an unusually rigid equality case: rank may not remain constant along a nontrivial transition.

The limiting rank need not be $K$. A run may repeatedly choose fixing outcomes below capacity while ignoring an improving outcome. Different runs from the same initial cycle may converge to different limits. The theorem proves convergence run by run, not confluence or global optimality.

\section{Future work}

The natural rank should be generalized to partial orders satisfying the ascending-chain condition. Exact plateaus may be replaced by metric estimates in which small gains force small revisions; summable gains could then yield Cauchy convergence without eventual identity. Fair exploration could promote selected-outcome fixedness to universal fixedness. Ordinal-indexed runs could include coherent limit stages. Finite instances could provide computable certificates and visual traces. Finally, cycles may be interpreted as theories and outcomes as certificates, with plateau stability derived from an extensional semantics rather than assumed.

\section{Conclusion}

A self-modifying process can change the evidence relevant to its next step while obeying a simple global convergence law. Dependence governs meaning, order governs termination, and topology records the result. Monotone bounded quality reaches an attained maximum; plateau stability lifts stationary rank to stationary state; eventual equality then gives convergence in every discrete topology. Heterogeneous reflective dynamics are therefore tractable whenever every genuine revision spends one unit of a finite progress resource.

from typing import Callable, Iterable, Sequence

    protocol: str

    step: int
    before: Cycle
    outcome: int
    admissible_count: int
    after: Cycle


def admissible_outcomes(cycle: Cycle, capacity: int) -> range:
    """Return gains meaningful at this cycle: 0 through remaining capacity."""
    if not 0 <= cycle.quality <= capacity:
        raise ValueError("cycle quality must lie between zero and capacity")
    return range(capacity - cycle.quality + 1)


def revise(cycle: Cycle, gain: int, capacity: int) -> Cycle:
    """Apply an admissible gain, changing protocol only on strict improvement."""
    if gain not in admissible_outcomes(cycle, capacity):
        raise ValueError(f"gain {gain} is inadmissible at quality {cycle.quality}")
    if gain == 0:
        return cycle
    new_quality = cycle.quality + gain
    return Cycle(new_quality, f"protocol-q{new_quality}")


def simulate(
    initial: Cycle, gains: Iterable[int], capacity: int
) -> tuple[list[Cycle], list[TraceRow]]:
    """Generate a dependent run and record its changing outcome-space sizes."""
    cycles = [initial]
    rows: list[TraceRow] = []
    current = initial
    for step, gain in enumerate(gains):
        choices = admissible_outcomes(current, capacity)
        nxt = revise(current, gain, capacity)
        rows.append(TraceRow(step, current, gain, len(choices), nxt))
        cycles.append(nxt)
        current = nxt
    return cycles, rows


def verify_trace(cycles: Sequence[Cycle], capacity: int) -> None:
    """Check boundedness, monotonicity, and plateau stability on a finite trace."""
    if not cycles:
        raise ValueError("a trace must contain at least one cycle")
    for cycle in cycles:
        assert 0 <= cycle.quality <= capacity
    for before, after in zip(cycles, cycles[1:]):
        assert before.quality <= after.quality
        if before.quality == after.quality:
            assert before == after


def stabilization_index(cycles: Sequence[Cycle]) -> int:
    """Find the earliest index after which the supplied finite trace is constant."""
    if not cycles:
        raise ValueError("a trace must contain at least one cycle")
    final = cycles[-1]
    index = len(cycles) - 1
    while index > 0 and cycles[index - 1] == final:
        index -= 1
    return index

    """Return K-q(c_0), the theorem's bound on genuine state changes."""
    if not 0 <= initial.quality <= capacity:
        raise ValueError("initial quality must lie between zero and capacity")
    return capacity - initial.quality


def greedy_gain(cycle: Cycle, capacity: int) -> int:
    """Choose the largest admissible gain."""
    return capacity - cycle.quality


def cautious_gain(cycle: Cycle, capacity: int) -> int:
    """Choose a unit gain until capacity, then choose the fixing outcome zero."""
    return 1 if cycle.quality < capacity else 0


def run_policy(
    initial: Cycle,
    capacity: int,
    policy: Callable[[Cycle, int], int],
    steps: int,
) -> list[Cycle]:
    """Run a state-dependent policy for a fixed reporting horizon."""
    current = initial
    result = [current]
    for _ in range(steps):
        current = revise(current, policy(current, capacity), capacity)
        result.append(current)
    return result

    capacity = 8
    initial = Cycle(1, "protocol-q1")
    cycles, rows = simulate(initial, [2, 1, 3, 1, 0, 0], capacity)
    verify_trace(cycles, capacity)
    print("\nDEMO 1 — Dependent outcome spaces")
    print("step | quality before | chosen gain | admissible gains | quality after")
    for row in rows:

            f"{allowed:>16} | {row.after.quality:>13}"

    print("trajectory:", [cycle.quality for cycle in cycles])
    print("stabilization index in this prefix:", stabilization_index(cycles))


def demo_revision_bound() -> None:
    """Compare observed strict changes with the finite-capacity bound."""
    capacity = 10
    initial = Cycle(3, "protocol-q3")
    cycles, _ = simulate(initial, [1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 0, 0], capacity)
    verify_trace(cycles, capacity)
    strict_changes = sum(a != b for a, b in zip(cycles, cycles[1:]))
    bound = strict_revision_bound(initial, capacity)
    print("\nDEMO 2 — Strict-revision budget")
    print("qualities:", [cycle.quality for cycle in cycles])
    print(f"observed genuine changes: {strict_changes}; theorem bound: {bound}")
    assert strict_changes <= bound


def demo_policy_comparison() -> None:
    """Show distinct transient paths with the same eventual fixed cycle."""
    capacity = 6
    initial = Cycle(0, "protocol-q0")
    greedy = run_policy(initial, capacity, greedy_gain, 8)
    cautious = run_policy(initial, capacity, cautious_gain, 10)
    verify_trace(greedy, capacity)
    verify_trace(cautious, capacity)
    print("\nDEMO 3 — Policy comparison")
    print("greedy qualities: ", [cycle.quality for cycle in greedy])
    print("cautious qualities:", [cycle.quality for cycle in cautious])
    print("both tails are fixed at capacity:", greedy[-1] == cautious[-1])


def main() -> None:
    """Run all three demonstrations."""
    demo_dependent_outcomes()
    demo_revision_bound()
    demo_policy_comparison()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The examples model a cycle by a quality rank and a protocol label.  Outcomes

strict rank increase; a zero gain leaves the entire cycle unchanged.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Sequence


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cycle:
    """A research cycle with bounded quality and a descriptive protocol."""

    quality: int
    protocol: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceRow:
    """One transition and the size of its state-dependent outcome space."""

    step: int
    before: Cycle
    outcome: int
    admissible_count: int
    after: Cycle


def admissible_outcomes(cycle: Cycle, capacity: int) -> range:
    """Return gains meaningful at this cycle: 0 through remaining capacity."""
    if not 0 <= cycle.quality <= capacity:
        raise ValueError("cycle quality must lie between zero and capacity")
    return range(capacity - cycle.quality + 1)


def revise(cycle: Cycle, gain: int, capacity: int) -> Cycle:
    """Apply an admissible gain, changing protocol only on strict improvement."""
    if gain not in admissible_outcomes(cycle, capacity):
        raise ValueError(f"gain {gain} is inadmissible at quality {cycle.quality}")
    if gain == 0:
        return cycle
    new_quality = cycle.quality + gain
    return Cycle(new_quality, f"protocol-q{new_quality}")


def simulate(
    initial: Cycle, gains: Iterable[int], capacity: int
) -> tuple[list[Cycle], list[TraceRow]]:
    """Generate a dependent run and record its changing outcome-space sizes."""
    cycles = [initial]
    rows: list[TraceRow] = []
    current = initial
    for step, gain in enumerate(gains):
        choices = admissible_outcomes(current, capacity)
        nxt = revise(current, gain, capacity)
        rows.append(TraceRow(step, current, gain, len(choices), nxt))
        cycles.append(nxt)
        current = nxt
    return cycles, rows


def verify_trace(cycles: Sequence[Cycle], capacity: int) -> None:
    """Check boundedness, monotonicity, and plateau stability on a finite trace."""
    if not cycles:
        raise ValueError("a trace must contain at least one cycle")
    for cycle in cycles:
        assert 0 <= cycle.quality <= capacity
    for before, after in zip(cycles, cycles[1:]):
        assert before.quality <= after.quality
        if before.quality == after.quality:
            assert before == after


def stabilization_index(cycles: Sequence[Cycle]) -> int:
    """Find the earliest index after which the supplied finite trace is constant."""
    if not cycles:
        raise ValueError("a trace must contain at least one cycle")
    final = cycles[-1]
    index = len(cycles) - 1
    while index > 0 and cycles[index - 1] == final:
        index -= 1
    return index

    """Return K-q(c_0), the theorem's bound on genuine state changes."""
    if not 0 <= initial.quality <= capacity:
        raise ValueError("initial quality must lie between zero and capacity")
    return capacity - initial.quality

    return capacity - cycle.quality


def cautious_gain(cycle: Cycle, capacity: int) -> int:
    """Choose a unit gain until capacity, then choose the fixing outcome zero."""
    return 1 if cycle.quality < capacity else 0

import Mathlib

/-!
# Rota's basis conjecture in ranks one and two

Rota's basis conjecture is open in full generality.  This file gives a faithful
formalization using Mathlib's `Basis` and proves the conjecture for one and two
bases.  An arrangement records that every row is a permutation of the given
basis and that every column is linearly independent.  Since the columns have
exactly as many entries as the ambient dimension, `columnBasis` upgrades each
column to a Mathlib `Basis`.
-/

namespace Catalog.Combinatorics.RotaBasis

open Module

variable {K V : Type*} [DivisionRing K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]

/-- A Rota arrangement: rows permute the supplied bases and columns are
linearly independent. -/
def IsRotaArrangement {n : ℕ} (B : Fin n → Basis (Fin n) K V)
    (G : Fin n → Fin n → V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, ∃ e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), G i = fun j => B i (e j)) ∧
    ∀ j, LinearIndependent K (fun i => G i j)

/-- Every column of a Rota arrangement canonically determines a basis. -/
noncomputable def columnBasis {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (B : Fin n → Basis (Fin n) K V)
    (G : Fin n → Fin n → V) (hG : IsRotaArrangement B G) (j : Fin n) :
    Basis (Fin n) K V :=
  basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank (hG.2 j) (by
    rw [Fintype.card_fin, Module.finrank_eq_card_basis (B 0), Fintype.card_fin])

@[simp] theorem columnBasis_apply {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (B : Fin n → Basis (Fin n) K V)
    (G : Fin n → Fin n → V) (hG : IsRotaArrangement B G) (j i : Fin n) :
    columnBasis B G hG j i = G i j := by
  simp [columnBasis]

/-- Rota's basis conjecture in dimension one. -/
theorem rota_basis_rank_one (B : Fin 1 → Basis (Fin 1) K V) :
    ∃ G, IsRotaArrangement B G := by
  use fun i j => B i j
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact ⟨Equiv.refl _, rfl⟩
  · intro j
    have hj : B 0 j ≠ 0 := (B 0).ne_zero j
    rw [Fintype.linearIndependent_iff]
    intro g hg
    simp only [Fin.sum_univ_one] at hg
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    exact Or.resolve_right (smul_eq_zero.mp hg) hj

    (hcd : LinearIndependent K (![c, d] : Fin 2 → V)) :

      LinearIndependent K (![b, d] : Fin 2 → V)) ∨
    (LinearIndependent K (![a, d] : Fin 2 → V) ∧
      LinearIndependent K (![b, c] : Fin 2 → V)) := by
  rw [LinearIndependent.pair_iff] at hab hcd
  simp only [LinearIndependent.pair_iff]
  by_cases hac : ∀ (s t : K), s • a + t • c = 0 → s = 0 ∧ t = 0
  · by_cases hbd : ∀ (s t : K), s • b + t • d = 0 → s = 0 ∧ t = 0
    · left; exact ⟨hac, hbd⟩
    · right
      -- b, d are NOT linearly independent, so d = m • b for some m

      obtain ⟨s, t, hst, hst_ne⟩ := hbd

    (G : Fin n → Fin n → V) (hG : IsRotaArrangement B G) (j : Fin n) :
    Basis (Fin n) K V :=
  basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank (hG.2 j) (by
    rw [Fintype.card_fin, Module.finrank_eq_card_basis (B 0), Fintype.card_fin])

On a finite sample space, this file studies the normalized weights

`exp(a) * log(b * xᵢ + 1)`.

corresponding row and column of the Fisher matrix vanish, and the two-parameter

open scoped BigOperators

def activation (x : ι → ℝ) (b : ℝ) (i : ι) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (b * x i + 1)

/-- The total logarithmic activation. -/
def activationMass (x : ι → ℝ) (b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, activation x b i

/-- The unnormalized exp-log weight of sample `i`. -/
def rawWeight (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (i : ι) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp a * activation x b i

/-- The partition function of the finite exp-log model. -/
def partition (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, rawWeight x a b i

/-- The normalized exp-log probability weight. -/
def probability (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (i : ι) : ℝ :=
  rawWeight x a b i / partition x a b

/-- The partition function factors into the exponential scale and activation mass. -/
theorem partition_factor (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) :
    partition x a b = Real.exp a * activationMass x b := by
  simp [partition, rawWeight, activationMass, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- Positive inputs and a positive shape parameter give positive activations. -/

    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (i : ι) :

  apply Real.log_pos
  dsimp [activation]
  nlinarith [mul_pos hb (hx i)]

/-- On a nonempty sample space, positive inputs give positive activation mass. -/

    (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) :

  apply Finset.sum_pos
  · intro i _
    exact activation_pos x b hb hx i
  · exact Finset.univ_nonempty

/-- Normalization cancels the exponential scale parameter exactly. -/
theorem probability_scale_cancels (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    probability x a b i = activation x b i / activationMass x b := by
  rw [probability, partition_factor]
  unfold rawWeight
  field_simp [Real.exp_ne_zero, hmass]

theorem probability_independent_of_scale (x : ι → ℝ) (a₁ a₂ b : ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    probability x a₁ b i = probability x a₂ b i := by
  rw [probability_scale_cancels x a₁ b i hmass,
    probability_scale_cancels x a₂ b i hmass]

  simp_rw [probability_scale_cancels x a b _ hmass]

theorem scaleScore_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)

  have hp : partition x a b ≠ 0 := by
    rw [partition_factor]
    exact mul_ne_zero (Real.exp_ne_zero a) hmass
  simp [scaleScore, hp]

def fisherAA (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, probability x a b i * scaleScore x a b ^ 2

/-- The Fisher information of the scale parameter is zero. -/
theorem fisherAA_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherAA x a b = 0 := by
  simp [fisherAA, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

def fisherScaleAgainst (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (score : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, probability x a b i * scaleScore x a b * score i

/-- Every mixed Fisher term involving the redundant scale direction vanishes. -/
theorem fisherScaleAgainst_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (score : ι → ℝ)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherScaleAgainst x a b score = 0 := by
  simp [fisherScaleAgainst, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The two-parameter Fisher matrix, with the true scale score in coordinate zero
and an arbitrary candidate score for the shape parameter in coordinate one. -/
def fisherMatrix (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) :
    Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℝ :=
  fun j k => ∑ i, probability x a b i *
    (if j = 0 then scaleScore x a b else shapeScore i) *
    (if k = 0 then scaleScore x a b else shapeScore i)

/-- The determinant of the two-parameter Fisher matrix. -/
def fisherDeterminant (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 0 * fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 1 1 -
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 1 * fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 1 0

/-- The scale row of the Fisher matrix is zero. -/
theorem fisherMatrix_scale_row_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) (k : Fin 2) :
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 k = 0 := by
  simp [fisherMatrix, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The scale column of the Fisher matrix is zero. -/
theorem fisherMatrix_scale_column_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) (j : Fin 2) :
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore j 0 = 0 := by
  simp [fisherMatrix, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The two-parameter Fisher matrix is singular for every possible shape score. -/
theorem fisherDeterminant_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherDeterminant x a b shapeScore = 0 := by
  simp [fisherDeterminant, fisherMatrix_scale_row_zero x a b shapeScore hmass]

  · intro hv

theorem scaleScore_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    scaleScore x a b = 0 := by
  have hp : partition x a b ≠ 0 := by
    rw [partition_factor]
    exact mul_ne_zero (Real.exp_ne_zero a) hmass
  simp [scaleScore, hp]

/-- The Fisher information in the exponential scale direction. -/
def fisherAA (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, probability x a b i * scaleScore x a b ^ 2

/-- The Fisher information of the scale parameter is zero. -/
theorem fisherAA_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherAA x a b = 0 := by
  simp [fisherAA, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The Fisher pairing between the scale score and an arbitrary second score. -/
def fisherScaleAgainst (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (score : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, probability x a b i * scaleScore x a b * score i

/-- Every mixed Fisher term involving the redundant scale direction vanishes. -/
theorem fisherScaleAgainst_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (score : ι → ℝ)
    (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherScaleAgainst x a b score = 0 := by
  simp [fisherScaleAgainst, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The two-parameter Fisher matrix, with the true scale score in coordinate zero
and an arbitrary candidate score for the shape parameter in coordinate one. -/
def fisherMatrix (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) :
    Fin 2 → Fin 2 → ℝ :=
  fun j k => ∑ i, probability x a b i *
    (if j = 0 then scaleScore x a b else shapeScore i) *
    (if k = 0 then scaleScore x a b else shapeScore i)

/-- The determinant of the two-parameter Fisher matrix. -/
def fisherDeterminant (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 0 * fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 1 1 -
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 1 * fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 1 0

/-- The scale row of the Fisher matrix is zero. -/
theorem fisherMatrix_scale_row_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) (k : Fin 2) :
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore 0 k = 0 := by
  simp [fisherMatrix, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The scale column of the Fisher matrix is zero. -/
theorem fisherMatrix_scale_column_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) (j : Fin 2) :
    fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore j 0 = 0 := by
  simp [fisherMatrix, scaleScore_eq_zero x a b hmass]

/-- The two-parameter Fisher matrix is singular for every possible shape score. -/
theorem fisherDeterminant_eq_zero (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    fisherDeterminant x a b shapeScore = 0 := by
  simp [fisherDeterminant, fisherMatrix_scale_row_zero x a b shapeScore hmass]

/-- The Fisher quadratic form vanishes on the nonzero scale-coordinate vector,
so it cannot be positive definite on the proposed two-parameter space. -/
theorem fisher_not_positive_definite (x : ι → ℝ) (a b : ℝ)
    (shapeScore : ι → ℝ) (hmass : activationMass x b ≠ 0) :
    ∃ v : Fin 2 → ℝ, v ≠ 0 ∧
      ∑ j, ∑ k, v j * fisherMatrix x a b shapeScore j k * v k = 0 := by
  refine ⟨fun j => if j = 0 then 1 else 0, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hv
    have hzero := congrFun hv 0
    simp at hzero
  · simp [fisherMatrix_scale_column_zero x a b shapeScore hmass]
